title: A Belfast boy grows up to define absolute zero
episode: The Life and Science of Lord Kelvin
place: Lord Kelvin’s birthplace, College Square East
description: William Thomson, later Lord Kelvin, was born on College Square East in 1824 and went on to set the absolute temperature scale and help lay the first working transatlantic telegraph cable. A plaque marks the house; his statue stands in Botanic Gardens.

title: Titanic on film in the Belfast shipyard, 1912
description: Surviving film of RMS Titanic at Harland & Wolff in Belfast in 1912, before it left for Southampton. The liner was fitted out at the Thompson Dry Dock, which still stands on Queen’s Road beside its pump house.

title: Where the Titanic and Olympic were built, then and now
description: Archive images of Harland & Wolff shipyard set against the same ground today, where the Titanic Belfast museum, opened in 2012, stands at the head of the slipways that built Titanic and its sister ship Olympic.

title: The firm behind the shipyard’s drawing offices
episode: The Shipyard That Built Titanic: Harland & Wolff
description: A history of Harland & Wolff, founded in 1861 by Edward Harland and Gustav Wolff and once the world’s largest shipyard. Titanic was designed in its headquarters drawing offices, now the Titanic Hotel.

title: A boss rigger remembers forty years at Harland & Wolff
episode: Titanic: George McAllister, Boss Rigger at Harland & Wolff, 1948 - 1992
description: George McAllister, a rigger at Harland & Wolff from 1948 to 1992, recalls shipyard work in its later decades, the era when the yard put up Samson and Goliath, the yellow gantry cranes that still dominate the Belfast skyline.

title: The DeLorean factory shuts down in 1982
description: Archive news of the end of production at John DeLorean’s car plant in Dunmurry on Belfast’s southwestern edge, which began building cars with British government money in 1981 and stopped in 1982 after the company went into receivership.

title: A footballer from the Cregagh estate
episode: George Best The Genius of Belfast & Manchester United Legend
description: George Best grew up on the Cregagh housing estate in east Belfast before Manchester United signed him at 15. This profile follows his career; a mural on the estate now marks the family home on Burren Way.

title: A black cab ride past the Falls Road murals
episode: Belfast, Northern Ireland: A Black Cab Tour of Falls Road - Rick Steves’ Europe Travel Guide
description: Travel writer Rick Steves rides a black taxi up the Falls Road, the main street of Catholic, nationalist west Belfast, past political murals and memorials to the Troubles, the 30-year conflict over Northern Ireland’s status.

title: Orange sashes and bowler hats on parade
episode: Belfast, Northern Ireland: Orangemen Parades - Rick Steves’ Europe Travel Guide - Travel Bite
description: Rick Steves watches an Orange Order parade, the Protestant fraternity’s marches with bands and banners that peak on the Twelfth of July, marking William of Orange’s 1690 victory. Belfast’s main parade passes City Hall.

title: A wall between neighbours on Cupar Way
description: A short documentary on one of Belfast’s peace walls, the barriers built between Catholic and Protestant streets during the Troubles. The tallest, on Cupar Way between the Shankill and the Falls, is covered in messages from visitors.

title: Inside the Victorian jail on Crumlin Road
episode: Inside Belfast's Most Famous Prison (Crumlin Road Gaol)
description: A walk through Crumlin Road Gaol, opened in 1845 to Charles Lanyon’s design and closed in 1996. It held suffragettes, republican and loyalist prisoners, and carried out 17 executions; a tunnel links it to the courthouse opposite.

title: Saturday stalls under a Victorian roof
episode: St. George's Market in Belfast: Walk Through
description: A walk through St George’s Market, Belfast’s last surviving Victorian covered market, built 1890–96, where weekend stalls sell Ulster fries, fresh fish from the County Down ports, soda farls and local cheese.
